PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mechanical Properties of Materials? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Mechanical Properties of Materials.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Waves? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Waves.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Waves.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Waves.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Moments and equilibrium? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Moments and equilibrium.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Moments and equilibrium.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Moments and equilibrium.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Energy, Work, Power and Machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Waves and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.

3. A — Ice melting to water

4. D — Glucose and oxygen

5. D — 100 °C

6. D — newton (N)

7. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Energy, Work, Power and Machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
